headline: Executive order keeps in place the suspension of duty-free entry for low-value imported packages from all countries.
what_it_does: Based on its title, this order continues an existing pause on "de minimis" treatment. That rule had let low-value packages shipped into the US skip import duties (taxes on imports). Continuing the suspension means these packages still owe duties, no matter which country they come from. No summary was provided, so the specific details of the order are not known.

who_it_affects.group: People in the US who buy low-cost goods online from overseas sellers
who_it_affects.how: Their packages may still owe import duties instead of arriving duty-free.

who_it_affects.group: Overseas sellers and online retailers that ship small orders directly to US customers
who_it_affects.how: Their small shipments to the US remain subject to duties.

who_it_affects.group: Shipping companies, postal services, and customs brokers
who_it_affects.how: They continue to handle duty collection and customs paperwork for low-value packages.
